tier_reason: First-party Daint GH200 campaign (benchmarks/daint/fair_t72_summary.md, campaign 2b755997) with public drivers (benchmarks/sweep_fair.py, benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt) and every claimed ratio and win count present; but the page states no compiler or flags, and the toolchain column in benchmarks/daint/results.csv belongs to a later snapshot that does not include campaign 2b755997, so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated on the benchmark page. The later Daint snapshot (benchmarks/daint/results.csv, not the 2b755997 campaign the headline ratios come from) records Clang 22.1.8 with libomp for CPU apxchol rows, GCC 14.3 for GPU GKS rows and NVCC with GCC 14.3 host for GPU trace rows; competitor rows say only 'clang' or 'julia'. Build is CMake Release with APXCHOL_NATIVE_ARCH on by default (-mcpu=native on ARM, -march=native on x86); exact flags of the measured binaries are not listed.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark by the library authors; the headline page is a labelled historical snapshot (campaign 2b755997) and not a measurement of current main, and its numbers differ from the refreshed benchmarks/daint/summary.md tables. The page does not say how per-matrix competitor/apxchol ratios are averaged. AMGCL beats apxchol on 16 of 26 CPU matrices in that campaign; the 1.735x CPU ratio over AMGCL comes mostly from interior-point and social-graph systems (in summary.md AMGCL takes 7.56-9.92 s on iter0020-iter0040 vs about 0.32 s, and 83.74 s vs 4.68 s on com-LiveJournal), while AMGCL is as fast or faster on grids, parabolic_fem, kron_g500-logn16 and com-Orkut. Pairs where a solver timed out, failed or did not converge are excluded from the ratios (hypre timed out on as-Skitter, com-LiveJournal, com-Orkut and com-Youtube on CPU). 'SuiteSparse' in the tables means matrices from the SuiteSparse Matrix Collection, not the SuiteSparse library; the baselines (hypre, AMGCL) are not SuiteSparse, Eigen sparse or PETSc. Licensed BSD-4-Clause (advertising clause), which is not OSI-approved, so usability is reference rather than copyable. Young repo (benchmark docs dated 2026-09).

notes: All claimed numbers (3.267x/23 of 23, 3.555x/25 of 25, 1.735x with 10 wins/16 losses vs AMGCL, GPU 2.028x/25 of 26 and 1.835x/22 of 26) are on fair_t72_summary.md. Fixed usability (BSD-4-Clause is not OSI-approved) and clarified that the compiler versions come from a later snapshot's CSV. Stars 8, 3 forks, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-09-30 all confirmed.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC (version not stated), CUDA toolkit (version not stated), CMake Release build per the SpBench README; SpBench benchmark code is public
corrections.caveats: Shootout (SpBench) written by cuBool's own author in 2021 (last SpBench commit 2021-09-04); the same tables are in the authors' peer-reviewed IPDPSW 2021 paper (https://github.com/YaccConstructor/articles/blob/master/2021/GRAPL/Sparse_Boolean_Algebra_on_GPGPU/Sparse_Boolean_Algebra_on_GPGPU.pdf), which reports each result as an average of 10 runs and says 'the comparison is not entirely fair'. It compares a GTX 1070 GPU against SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS on a 4-core i7-6700; SuiteSparse version and thread count are not stated. On road networks cuBool's mxm is slower than clBool and on luxembourg_osm also slower than cuSPARSE (2.4 vs 1.7 ms); its margin over SuiteSparse there is only 1.3-3.7x. For element-wise add, CUSP and cuSPARSE beat cuBool on every road matrix (roadNet-PA 16.9 ms vs CUSP 11.2 ms), as the paper itself notes. SuiteSparse here is the GraphBLAS component, not CHOLMOD or UMFPACK, so this is not a solver comparison. Minor table drift: web-Google SuiteSparse add is 77.2 ms in the paper vs 77.5 ms in the SpBench README.

notes: All claimed numbers match SpBench README rows 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 (mxm) and 2, 4 (add); 16x and 11x ratios are correctly marked derived. Upgraded to B on the IPDPSW 2021 paper (venue confirmed via WebSearch result for IEEE Xplore document 9460674; the PDF itself carries no venue line). MIT license, 27 stars, last commit 2025-11-17 confirmed.

tier_reason: First-party table in doc/MultifrontalQR.md driven by public test/bench_multifrontal_qr.cpp, but compiler, flags and CPU are not stated for the QR runs (clang 22 -O3 on a Ryzen 9 5950X appears only in doc/Parallelism.md for the bench_parallel runs), and the median gain is above 50x, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: MultifrontalQR factorization (including rank verification) is 5-6900x faster than Eigen::SparseQR over the 34 SuiteSparse-collection matrices both finished, median 59x per the page (about 56x recomputed from the displayed table, derived from page data); e.g. cell2 66.6 s vs 20 ms, swang2 3182 ms vs 7.7 ms, TSOPF_RS_b9_c6 32.5 s vs 4.7 ms, raefsky2 3095 ms vs 622 ms (the 5x low end). On the author's own setfos samples (separate table): DriftDiffusion n29841 8461 ms vs 0.52 ms. It also returns the right rank where Eigen::SparseQR does not (raefsky5: Eigen reports rank 622 of 6316). SupernodalLDLT is 6.5x faster than Eigen::SimplicialLDLT on lap3d 40^3 (doc/SupernodalLDLT.md).
corrections.workload: Sparse QR factorization time, single thread, on 38 SuiteSparse-collection matrices (34 finished by both; Eigen had 300 s per run), b = A*xTrue, MultifrontalQR best of 3 with rank verification included while Eigen::SparseQR (COLAMD ordering) is timed in a single run; plus six matrices from the author's own setfos application corpus.
corrections.caveats: Very new (docs dated from 2026-08), zero-star, one-author project; the GitHub description reads 'Sparse direct LU solvers based on Eigen, implemented with Claude Code'. All numbers are the author's own, from the repo's benchmark drivers (test/bench_multifrontal_qr.cpp, test/bench_setfos_samples.cpp); hardware and compiler are recorded in doc/Parallelism.md, not beside the QR table. bench_multifrontal_qr times Eigen::SparseQR once but MultifrontalQR as best of N. Eigen::SparseQR is a weak baseline (the docs say it never permutes rows, so it has huge fill and wrong rank on badly scaled matrices); there is no comparison against SuiteSparseQR (SPQR), the real incumbent for sparse QR. Three matrices where only Eigen timed out (as-caida, foldoc, onetone2) are excluded from the median. The page's stated median (59x) is slightly above what the displayed table gives (about 56x). SupernodalLU is typically 2-3x slower and denser than Eigen::SparseLU on general unsymmetric matrices (doc/SupernodalLU.md), though 2.4-2.6x faster on the large laoss FEM matrices, so the speedup claim applies mainly to QR and symmetric LDLT; SimplicialLDLT still wins analyze time by 2-3x.

notes: Range 5-6900x, median 59x, cell2, swang2 and raefsky5 rank all on doc/MultifrontalQR.md; the DriftDiffusion example comes from the separate setfos table, not the 34-matrix SuiteSparse set, so claimed_speedup was reworded. Name lists SupernodalLU, which is generally slower than Eigen::SparseLU; consider dropping it from the name. MPL-2.0, 0 stars, 106 commits, last commit 2026-09-29 confirmed.
